_about: Nitrogen (1) + methanol (2): mole fraction solubility of nitrogen at a nitrogen partial pressure of 101.325 kPa, 248.15-323.15 K, from Kretschmer, Nowakowska and Wiebe (1946), as compiled in IUPAC SDS Vol. 10.

source.citation: C. B. Kretschmer, J. Nowakowska, R. Wiebe, Solubility of oxygen and nitrogen in organic solvents from -25 to 50 C, Ind. Eng. Chem. 38 (1946) 506-509
source.access: The original article is not open; its values are compiled in IUPAC Solubility Data Series Vol. 10, Nitrogen and Air (R. Battino, ed., Pergamon, 1982; copyright IUPAC), which IUPAC publishes as open access at iupac.github.io
source.tables: IUPAC Solubility Data Series Vol. 10 (1982) p 180 (PDF p 225), prepared by P. L. Long and H. L. Clever; experimental values, x_1 x 10^3 column (the smoothed values of the same sheet are not used). Ostwald coefficients measured at a total pressure of 101.325 kPa; the compiler calculated the mole fraction for a partial pressure of 101.325 kPa assuming the Ostwald coefficient independent of pressure. Estimated error (authors): average deviation from the mean 0.3 %, maximum 0.9 %. Accepted by the evaluator (R. Battino, p 174, PDF p 219).
source.transcription: Read from the scanned page image (rendered at 110 dpi) and the PDF's text layer, which agree value by value. The person checking should compare each row with the page.

notes: x_1 is the mole fraction of nitrogen in the liquid at a partial pressure of nitrogen of 101.325 kPa (1 atm), as the compiler gives it; it is stored as p_1_kPa = 101.325 (the fit compares it with y_1 P of the bubble point at x_1). To be checked by a person against the page (AGENTS.md rule 4).
